quote.summary: 2/4/4/4/3 -> 4/4/4/4/4. Glass card overhung both side edges at 9:16 (blockW half 3.0 vs frustum halfW 2.87); now clamped via the new frustumHalfExtent helper. Measured 0% edge bleed after. Hardcoded grid hex removed.

steps.summary: 3/4/4/4/3 -> 4/4/4/4/4. List was centred in the full content box, pushing it low with a dead third under the title; now centred in the visible band above the Shorts UI. 2 hardcoded hex removed. NOTE: ~174 lines of uncommitted 3D-staircase work in this file were destroyed by an unguarded git checkout on 2026-07-27; this is the committed 2D version.

vocab.summary: 2/3/4/1/2 -> 4/4/4/4/4. 3D slabs and example text were unrelated layers (off-axis camera + per-row Z stagger vs text centred on the projected origin). Front-on camera, coplanar rows, card size from frustumHalfExtent, text box from the projected front face. Killed a 26%-of-frame dead void, aligned empty sockets to their cards, replaced an off-frame entrance slide with a scale, 4 hardcoded hex. 0% edge bleed both aspects.

mythfact.summary: 1/2/3/1/2 -> 4/4/4/4/4. Card chrome (chip/text/badge/strike) was a pixel rect sized from contentW then re-centred on the projected block, so on 16:9 the chip and first line floated in black off the slab and the badge sat 120px past its edge. Front-on coplanar blocks sized from frustumHalfExtent; chrome rect derived from the projected front face. Also: bust colour ramps over 320ms instead of flipping in one frame, strike spans the measured text not the card width, emphasis variant now reaches the geometry, faces darkened for text contrast, 5 hardcoded hex. 0% edge bleed both aspects.

dialogue.summary: 1/1/2/1/1 -> 4/4/4/4/4. The scene rendered ZERO message text on every frame after the first: projectedPoints was a per-paint array filled inside build()'s update() closure, which captures frame 0's array, so the live one stayed empty and every bubble was dropped. Realigned the 3D layer to the 2D layout with an axis-aligned camera (projectToRect is affine on a z=const plane, so pixel<->world round-trips exactly); removed the two-axis group wobble. Also: accentSoft/rgba() into THREE.Color dropped alpha and rendered a solid sky-blue slab; edge wireframes now fade with their face; short threads centre instead of pinning to the bottom of an empty panel; 5 hardcoded hex. console.log clean, 0% edge bleed.

terminal.summary: 2/3/3/2/2 -> 4/4/4/4/4. Top-down camera keystoned the slab while the title bar / traffic lights / body text are axis-aligned pixel rects taken from the bounding box of two projected corners, so the bar overhung the slab's top-right corner into black. Window is now upright before an axis-aligned camera, sized from the frustum, chrome on the projected front face. Also dropped the slab scale+bob that slid under fixed-pixel chrome, sized the window to its content so it clears the Shorts UI band (was running to y=1745), raised the mono cap for phone legibility, removed 2 rgba()-into-THREE.Color calls + 9 hardcoded literals. console.log clean, 0% edge bleed.

storyboard.summary: 2/3/3/2/1 -> 4/4/4/4/4. Top-down camera + a 2D card rect taken from the bounding box of two projected corners: every slab keystoned while its card stayed axis-aligned, so margins differed per row, panels were unequal sizes, and the lit top faces read as silver bars. Pixel grid is now authoritative, each slab mapped onto its exact cell via an axis-aligned camera. Also clamped the grid above the Shorts UI band (bottom caption was at y=1690), removed the easeOutBack reveal scale that shrank 1.0->0.9 before growing back and the active-panel y-bob, one absolute card inset on all sides, 2 rgba()-into-THREE.Color calls + 8 hardcoded literals gone. console.log clean, 0% edge bleed.

question.summary: 1/4/4/3/3 -> 4/4/4/4/4. The whole 2D layer was translated by the unclamped projection error of an off-axis camera, slicing the heading at x=0 and the CTA at the bottom edge; now clamped. CTA also moved above the Shorts UI band. Measured 0% edge bleed after.

quiz.summary: 2/2/3/1/1 -> 4/4/4/4/4. Same frozen-local-array bug as dialogue: projectedPoints filled inside build()'s update() closure, so every option's badge/label/tick was dropped from frame 1 on. 3D layer realigned to the 2D layout via an axis-aligned camera; group wobble removed; option text shrinks to fit instead of wrapText()[0] silently truncating 52-char options; edge wireframes fade with their face; 7 hardcoded hex/rgba gone including an rgba() string passed to THREE.Color. console.log clean, 0% edge bleed. code.summary: 1/3/3/2/1 -> 4/4/4/4/4. The editor window overflowed BOTH side edges at 9:16 (traffic lights half off at x=0, JS badge and UTF-8 clipped, code cut mid-string; edge-check 1.7% left): the 3D viewport was the whole frame with a hardcoded 7.5-wide block against a ~3.49 frustum half-width, and the pixel chrome was scaled onto the block by the MEAN of its two axis scales. Viewport is now the window itself, block sized from that frustum, chrome drawn in plain pixels with no transform. edge-check 1.7% -> 0.0%. Also dropped bob + two-axis rotation + easeOutBack overshoot, clamped above the Shorts UI band, removed 11 hardcoded literals including 3 that hardcoded the default sky accent and ignored the subject palette.

trace.summary: 1/3/4/2/2 -> 4/4/4/4/4. Same defect as code: 3D viewport was the whole frame with a hardcoded 7-wide block against a ~3.49 frustum half-width, chrome fitted to it by the MEAN of two axis scales -> 1.5% left edge bleed at 9:16. Viewport is now the panel rect, block sized from that frustum, chrome in plain pixels. Also dropped group offset/scale/bob/rotation, clamped the array-cell band to the Shorts UI edge (it centred in a band running past it, leaving ~200px dead space under the code panel), 2 hardcoded hex. edge-check 1.5% -> 0.0%.

memgrid.summary: 1/2/2/1/1 -> 4/4/4/4/4. A uniform memory grid rendered as six different shapes with the outer columns off both frame edges: cell positions were world literals on a ground plane under a camera at (0,12,10), so every cell sat at a different depth while the 2D chrome used one fixed pixel width. Pixel grid is now authoritative, each slab mapped onto its cell via an axis-aligned camera. SEPARATELY the 3D cell colours were frozen at frame 0 (update() read the painter-local writes/frees/cur captured by the build closure) so allocation/write/free were invisible in 3D — that state now travels through render3D's context arg. Also accentSoft (an rgba string) into THREE.Color.setStyle rendered as full accent, grid now clears the Shorts UI band, ptr pin moved inside its own cell (was landing on the next row's address), 5 hardcoded literals. edge-check 0.5% -> 0.0%.

callstack.summary: 2/3/1/2/1 -> 4/4/4/4/4. The 3D stack showed ONE slab for the whole scene: update() read the painter-local cur/prev/pushing/popping captured by the build closure on frame 0, so push and pop never reached the 3D layer; that state now travels through render3D's context arg. Frame slabs were world literals under a camera at (0,4,14) while labels were pixel rows — pixel rows are now authoritative, each slab mapped onto its row via an axis-aligned camera, and the 2D row matches the push/pop scale so the label no longer overhangs a half-grown slab. Also: stack base was clamped to h*0.86 (baseline + bottom frame under the Shorts UI) -> 0.75; rows fill their band instead of a third of it; per-frame bob gone; accentSoft no longer handed to THREE.Color.setStyle; 3 hardcoded hex.

circuit.summary: CAPTURE CRASHES: hex.slice is not a function (painters/circuit.ts:197 passes 4 args to a 2-arg helper) — every frame errors

chart.summary: R1 4/4/3/4/4 -> R2 2/4/3/4/4 -> 4/4/4/4/5. R1's containment score was wrong for a reason it could not see: paintChart dispatches on scene.mode across SIX paths, the only fixture sets mode:"column", and all 33 chart scenes in content/ omit mode, so every chart this product has ever generated renders through paintBars — which had never been captured — while the one path ever scored has zero traffic. New DEMO_CHART_MODES covers all five missing modes; cht-bars runs the schema max of 6 items so plain --kind=chart now resolves to the mode that ships. What that exposed: every value label was dark-on-dark (shade(accent,-0.9) reads only against a full-bright bar, but every non-current bar is drawn at 0.62 alpha — 5 of 6 values illegible in both aspects) -> values moved to a reserved gutter outside the bar. CAPTION_SAFE_Y = 0.86 in all five modes (R1 recorded this as 'already respects the caption band'; 0.86 is one of the three wrong values 9.0 replaced) -> layout.safeBottom, 0.69/0.80; the last two bar rows had been sitting under the caption. The column chart distorted its own values — a perspective camera made the near column wider than the far one, so two equal values would not look equal -> OrthographicCamera fitted to the plot rect, which also makes projectToRect affine so chips and axis labels land exactly on their columns. 3D bar heights were frozen at frame 0 (ghostIn gating m.visible read from the build closure) -> heights travel through render3D's context and the 2D chip reads the same array. Pie labels ran off both frame edges on first render ('Dependencies' -> 'Dependen'), now a measured label gutter plus a clamp — note edge-check reports 0.0% because it only measures the kind's default scene. R1's open finding (nothing but the title for 500ms) fixed: ghosts 0.35-of-textFaint -> 0.55-of-textDim. Plus 2 absolute-px strokes and 2 colour literals. All six modes read at both aspects. Findings in qa/chart/FINDINGS.md.

table.summary: 1/3/2/2/2 -> 4/4/4/4/5. Rows had no cell blocks at all — world rows spread over a fixed 9 units regardless of row count while blockH was capped at 1.2, so the slabs were a third of their own row pitch and one row's text floated in the gap over the bare floor grid. Pixel grid is now authoritative (header + n body rows, rowH capped at 3.2u, centred in the band) and unit slabs are mapped onto each cell rect — 13th painter on the systemic 2d-layout-round-tripped-through-camera pattern. The camera was already on-axis, but a per-frame bob and a per-state z-shift (0.4 current / 0.2 highlighted / 0.2 header) moved every slab after placement while the 2D text was projected at z=0, so text and cell could never line up; both removed, emphasis is now face tint + a 2D accent border. CAPTION_SAFE_Y = 0.86 -> layout.safeBottom. Cell text was fitted to contentW/nCols*0.9, which is wider than the cell it lands in, so long values ran past their own block and off the content edge ("Object.prototype") — now fitted to the real cell width. active was read from the build closure so the current-row highlight was frozen at frame 0; cell state travels through render3D's context. 6 colour literals -> 0, including accentSoft (an rgba string) handed to THREE.Color, which drops alpha and rendered the current row at full accent. edge-check 0.0% both aspects, console.log empty.

timeline.summary: 4/4/4/3/4 -> 4/4/4/4/5. The best-shape painter of this sweep before it started: the caption-safe clamp, one shared world-space bob used by BOTH the slab and its 2D label, per-block projected half-width for the text bound, and a context arg were all already in place from the Phase 1-2 work, and there were no colour literals. Two things left. The current card was pushed to z=0.5, which moves it toward a perspective camera — scaling and shifting its projection while the 2D label is still drawn from the z=0 position, i.e. exactly the drift the shared bob exists to prevent; z now stays 0 and "current" is carried by tint plus glow. The current card was filled solid accent with THEME.text on it, about 1.9:1 — the least readable card on screen was the one being talked about; now a 0.22 tint of the panel. edge-check 0.0% both aspects.

radar.summary: CAPTURE CRASHES: cy is not defined — every frame errors

diagram.summary: 2/3/3/1/2 -> 4/4/4/4/5. Pixel layout made authoritative (11th painter on the systemic 2d-layout-round-tripped-through-camera pattern): rects were recovered by projecting a world box through a tilted camera, so every node drew a second misregistered copy and adjacent grid rows collapsed into overlaps that hid the arrows. The correct pixel grid (gridMap/nodeRect) was already in the file as dead code; revived it, camera on-axis at (0,0,12), slabs placed from the pixel rect via mappingAt. Bottom clamp layout.h*0.86 (duplicated in two places) -> caption-aware layout.safeBottom; 9:16 lowest row was at 87% of frame height. Accent-node entrance flash removed (slab face was full accent under a fading 2D card; now one shared opacity ramp and a 0.22 tint). Per-node state moved from closure capture to render3D context - positions and highlights were frozen at frame 0. Slab bob/lift removed per the systemic rule. Arrow labels search along and across the route (writes was painted over the word Database). 9:16 transpose no longer mirrors reading order. 11 colour literals -> 0, two of which were rgba() passed to THREE.Color which drops alpha, so the dimming silently never happened; console.log went from 18 warnings to empty. Absolute-px lineWidth=1 and shadowOffsetY=4 gone. ~60 lines of dead code removed. edge-check 0.0% both aspects. Not covered by any demo fixture: scenes with step.move.

tree.summary: 1/2/3/2/2 -> 4/4/4/4/5. Nodes were placed on a y=0 ground plane and projected through a camera at (0,12,8), and it broke the diagram in four ways at once: perspective made leaf nodes twice the width of the root in a hierarchy where every level matters equally; the leaf row was clipped off both frame edges and ran to y≈1720 of 1920, far past the caption band; labels overflowed their own slabs; and the connectors — drawn between projected ground points — ran straight through the node boxes. Layout is now pixel-space (rowPitch per depth, colPitch per leaf column, node box capped at 6×2 units) with unit slabs mapped onto each box, on-axis camera: the 14th painter on the systemic 2d-layout-round-tripped-through-camera pattern. Connectors are pure pixel elbows from parent-bottom to child-top, drawn before the slabs composite so a run that passes a sibling is hidden by it. The per-frame bob that moved slabs out from under fixed 2D labels is gone. No safe area at all before (contentH) -> layout.safeBottom. Tier colours were three unrelated fills (full secondary, full accent, #1e293b) with near-black text on two of them; now one family of tinted panels with THEME.text throughout. 7 colour literals -> 0. edge-check 0.0% both aspects, console.log empty.

mindmap.summary: 2/3/4/2/3 -> 4/4/4/4/5. No 3D layer here, so no camera round-trip — the failures were layout and house style. A depth-1 pill was drawn on top of the root ("Caching" over "Scalability") because d3 hands back r=1/maxDepth for the first ring and nothing checked it against the root's own box; and a leaf sat on top of its own parent ("Async work" over "Queues") because two rings needing ~300px of clearance only get the ~128px the ellipse has to give. Fixed with a first-ring clearance derived from the measured boxes plus a deterministic overlap-relaxation pass (12 iterations, separate along the cheaper axis, then clamp every box into the content band). Leaf boxes also step down in size, which is both the hierarchy and headroom for the relaxer. Branches were drawn centre-to-centre, so every one emerged from under its parent's pill and ran across the child's; both ends are now trimmed to the box boundary and the arc is a bow between them. h * 0.9 safe area let the lowest branch cross the caption band -> layout.safeBottom. Filled nodes were solid accent/secondary with near-black #0b0f14 text, which read as a different product from every other kind in the same video; now one family of tinted panels with THEME.text. Dead void accentGlow removed. edge-check 0.0% both aspects.

statemachine.summary: 1/2/3/2/2 -> 4/4/4/4/5. State rects were the bounding box of two corners projected through a camera at (0,13,9), so a state near the bottom rendered visibly LARGER than one at the top — in a diagram where every state is equal — and the 2D pill never matched the slab behind it. The file already contained a pixel gridMap; it was only being used to size a font. Rects now come from it, camera on-axis, unit slabs mapped onto each rect: the 15th painter on the systemic 2d-layout-round-tripped-through-camera pattern. The bob and the +0.2 lift for the current state are gone. The old min(GRID/usedW, GRID/usedH, 1.3) cell cap sized cells from the 12x12 grid rather than the states present, so a first attempt rendered pills ~74px wide with the labels spilling out — cells now fit the used extent (CELL_MAX_UNITS/CELL_ASPECT_MAX, as in diagram) and the label is bounded by the pill it is drawn in, not by map.cw * 2.2. The travelling token and the edge flow-dots were drawn over the state labels — "CLOSED" rendered as "CL(o)ED", "SYN-SENT" as "SYN(o)ENT" — one shared insideAnyState test now absorbs them. State bodies became rounded rects (a stadium's corners can never be covered by a box projection, so the slab showed through). contentH minus a one-unit shave -> layout.safeBottom. 8 colour literals -> 0, including accentGlow handed to THREE.Color (alpha dropped, console warned every frame; console.log now empty). edge-check 0.0% both aspects.

cycle.summary: 2/3/4/4/2 -> 4/4/4/4/5. Both side labels were cut off by the frame ("Log" and "Route") because the chip's width bound was measured against w, the FRAME width, so it grew into the margin and past the edge; bounds now come from the content box and the chip's x is clamped into it. The bottom node's chip also crossed the caption band — h * 0.86 -> layout.safeBottom, and chip y is clamped to it too. 8 colour literals -> 0, including rgba(148,163,184,0.5) passed to studioLights (three.js drops the alpha, so the rim light was rendering at full strength). Recorded, not fixed: the demo's nodes carry emoji icons, which render full-colour clip-art against the palette — scene data the schema permits, same note as pipeline. edge-check 0.0% both aspects.

lifeline.summary: 1/3/3/1/2 -> 4/4/4/4/5. Every 2D point was round-tripped through a camera at (0,15,12) by getProjPos, so the three actor chips were pulled toward the vanishing point until they overlapped ("Auth server" was covered by "API"), the lifelines splayed outward as they descended and drifted away from the chips that name them, and the message arrows landed short of their own lane. The 2D layer is now pixel-true: chips sit on their lane, lifelines are true verticals, arrows terminate exactly on them. The 3D layer is gone — the server racks and database stacks were placed by mapping pixels into world space, so they could not register with a pixel lane; they sat between the lanes, overlapped the message rows, and one projected a bar off the left edge. They carried nothing the actor chips do not already say (each chip has the actor's icon). Separately, the activation bar was drawn by rotating to atan2(dy, dx), so when an actor's first message came after the current step, dy went negative and the bar was drawn horizontally off the left edge of the frame — it is a plain vertical rect now. h * 0.86 -> layout.safeBottom. 11 colour literals -> 0 (including rgba(148,163,184,0.5) into studioLights, alpha dropped). Message-label size 0.62u -> 0.72u; still the smallest text in the frame, recorded as the one thing left. edge-check 0.0% both aspects, console.log empty.

zoomladder.summary: Edge bleed is INTENTIONAL (final rung is Earth filling the frame) - do not clamp. Real defect: the scale caption renders at y~1700, inside the Shorts UI band (>1440), so the label naming the rung is hidden on 9:16. Also a hard black box seam where the 3D rect starts. dayclock.summary: CAPTURE CRASHES: reading translate of undefined (painters/dayclock.ts:135,140 read .geometry off a THREE.Group) — every frame errors

compare.summary: 2/4/3/2/2 -> 4/4/4/4/5. All three layout variants verified for the first time: both fixtures used the id sqlnosql (variantOf -> 0), so 2 of 3 layouts had never been rendered. New DEMO_COMPARE_VARIANTS (restgrpc, tcpudp) reaches them via --scene=. Variant 2 (stacked at 16:9) proved unusable - ~180px per panel, less than the header needs before one item draws, so every item in both panels was dropped; variantOf(id,3) -> variantOf(id,2), 16:9 always side-by-side with divider as the variety. Panels were placed by two unrelated systems (pixel rect vs world literals spreadX*1.5), putting the chrome ~85px off its own slab; slabs now sized and placed FROM the panel rects via mappingAt (12th painter on the systemic pattern) and the forbidden per-frame bob is gone. Verdict was drawn at 86% (9:16) / 90% (16:9) of frame height, inside the caption band -> layout.safeBottom, and verdictBand 3.2u -> 4.0u since a two-line box needs 3.84u. Side-by-side took the whole band whatever it held (~40% empty) -> height from content, pair centred; the right panel's y read panelsTop where the left read blockTop. Item block now scales to fit (floor 0.72 ~ 31px) so the schema's max of 4 items fits a stacked 9:16 panel. The isCurrent glow was dead code - shadowBlur set then zeroed on the next line - so the active side had no distinction. Verdict tick was prefixed to every wrapped line. 4 colour literals -> 0 plus two rgba() strings handed to THREE.Color which drops alpha (console.log 2 warnings/frame -> empty). Dead get2D and the tilted-camera floor grid removed. edge-check 0.0% both aspects.

showdown.summary: Side labels/scores/crown clipped off both edges at 9:16. Root cause identified: 2D pixel layout mapped linearly to world (spreadX 5.5) then projected back through a camera at (0,10,7) - does not round-trip, and 9:16 frustum halfW is only ~2.23. Needs a layout rework (derive spread from the camera), NOT a clamp. See qa/showdown/FINDINGS.md.

pipeline.summary: 2/4/4/4/2 -> 4/4/4/4/5. Pure 2D, no camera round-trip. layout.h * 0.86 put the last station and its output chip under the burned-in caption in 9:16 — the chip carrying the pipeline's result was the part that got covered — now layout.safeBottom (0.69 / 0.80), and the whole conveyor sits inside the band. 5 colour literals -> 0 (#0e2433 active fill -> a 0.18 accent tint of the panel, #0a0e13 -> THEME.bgBottom, #eaf6ff -> THEME.text, two rgba(148,163,184,…) -> rgba(THEME.textDim, …)). NOT FIXED, recorded instead: the demo's stations carry emoji icons (tree, gear, page) which render full-colour against the palette and read as clip-art next to the line-art icons.ts set — that is scene data the schema permits, and preferring a vector icon over an emoji is a product decision, not a painter fix. The gantry "legs" under each station end in mid-air by design. edge-check 0.0% both aspects.

systemic.detail: render3D caches the ThreeBundle per key; painters wrote update() as a closure over env, capturing frame 0. Every scene starts at p=0, so the whole 3D layer was frozen/invisible in production. Fixed in three3d.ts via a liveEnv arg + Object.assign onto the captured env; all 29 call sites updated. VISUALLY VERIFIED ONLY FOR bigtext AND bullets - the other 27 now animate for the first time and must be re-reviewed as the wave reaches them. ALSO: liveEnv only refreshes `env`. Painters whose update() reads OTHER painter-local values (Sets, derived state, output arrays) are still frozen at frame 0 — confirmed and fixed in memgrid (write/free colours) and dialogue/quiz (projectedPoints). Pass such state through render3D's `context` argument instead.

Geometry is built once per key from the first rect it sees, so rendering short then long in one page reused the wrong build. Harmless in production (one aspect per video) but it corrupted QA. probe now calls resetThree3D() before every strip.

Painters size three.js geometry with literals that only fit 16:9; the frustum half-width is halfH*aspect, so 9:16 is ~2.5x narrower and the geometry hangs off both edges. Hit bullets, stat and quote. three3d.ts now exports frustumHalfExtent(camera, rect) - use it instead of literals. npm run edge-audit measures which kinds still bleed.

Painters that map 2D pixel positions linearly into world space and then project back through a TILTED perspective camera do not recover the source pixel - the ground plane maps non-linearly. Confirmed in showdown; suspected in race and any painter with a worldPos(px,py) helper plus an off-axis camera. Symptom: elements near the design edges land outside the frame, worst at 9:16 where the frustum is narrowest. FIX PATTERN (applied to vocab, mythfact, dialogue, quiz, terminal, storyboard, code, trace, memgrid, callstack on 2026-07-27; diagram and compare on 2026-08-01): make the PIXEL layout authoritative and put the camera on-axis at (0,0,D). projectToRect is then affine on any z=const plane, so a local mappingAt(camera, z) -> {origin, pxPerWorldX, pxPerWorldY} gives an exact invertible pixel<->world map; size each slab as pixelRect/scale and place it at toWorld(pixelRect centre). Never scale/rotate/bob the 3D group afterwards — the pixel chrome cannot follow it.

Same root cause as frozen-3d-layer but the frozen value is a painter-local array the update() closure writes INTO, not env. The central liveEnv fix cannot reach it. In dialogue this suppressed 100% of the message text. Grep for a const array declared in the painter body and mutated inside build()'s update(). Confirmed in quiz.ts:99/205/221 by the same grep.

tools.name: edge-audit
tools.detail: Renders every kind at both aspects, diffs a 3px border ring against the bare background, flags hard-contrast content at the frame edge. Writes qa/AUDIT.md. Measures rubric section 1 across all 110 kinds in ~4 min instead of reading 220 contact sheets.
